# Threadbank: Vision and Roadmap

Status: Provisional proposal; not adopted. Evidence packet dated 2026-10-20–21. Review: author self-check only, at the operator's request; no independent review.

**Threadbank could help people turn existing costumes and remembered craft into new creative possibilities—so useful pieces, the knowledge behind them, and the ability to care for them survive from one production and volunteer generation to the next.**

The proposed destination is a living memory of costume reuse: makers can find pieces and understandable examples of adaptation, judge what suits their work, and leave useful knowledge for whoever comes next. It begins in our room and could become useful to other makers through voluntary, permissioned contributions. Its ambition is the creative capacity it preserves, not a required company, hosted service or audience size. This recommendation provisionally puts volunteer continuity and less waste ahead of income; the operator has not selected that ordering.

The path has three useful horizons:

| Horizon | What people gain | Evidence needed to continue |
|---|---|---|
| Make the room's memory dependable | A volunteer can find a plausible piece, see its promises and carry the records and photos to a successor, offline. | An unfamiliar volunteer completes a realistic retrieval and handoff exercise, including cases today's sampled receipts do not establish. |
| Make a past adaptation useful to someone else | A maker independently understands a documented alteration well enough to judge and try a suitable reuse. | Repeated transfer beyond the original author, with tolerable contribution effort and visible failed attempts. |
| Sustain a living body of reusable craft | Consenting makers can discover, adapt and maintain useful examples across time and, if desired, across groups. | Permission, stewardship and support can outlast an individual maintainer; usefulness persists outside the first demonstrations. |

Each horizon can stop

with something valuable. Multi-group borrowing is a separate future choice, not a hidden requirement of these horizons. This document proposes future work; it does not authorize implementation, partnerships, publication or adoption.

## Why this direction

Threadbank started because an already-made coat could not be found. The present room has roughly 900 pieces. In the supplied account, a volunteer found a suitable coat within minutes, photographs helped a director choose between two options, and fit was then checked in person. A different search failed because an adjustable garment was described with another term. The operator attributes one avoided purchase to the tool; there is no repeated timing or savings study. These are useful signs of value and a specific retrieval problem, not demonstrated benefits for every production. [E1, supplied observations](evidence/observations.md)

Finding stock is only part of the possible need. A maker reused a skirt after seeing an old show photograph, while alteration details stayed in someone else's notebook. Another maker wants accounts of how garments can change without losing their original work. The pivotal hypothesis is that understandable histories of adaptation could make existing materials useful in situations their catalogue labels never anticipated. It is not yet known whether other makers would use or contribute those histories. [E3](evidence/observations.md)

There is no externally established urgency. The opportunity is to preserve context while the people who know it can explain it, and to use a working local tool as a low-cost place to learn. The ability to maintain a quiet, understandable tool after its creator leaves matters in the supplied experience. Two current volunteers constrain pace; they do not define the permanent audience. [E4](evidence/observations.md), [operator brief](operator-brief.md)

Three futures deserve serious consideration:

| Product future | Concrete experience and distinctive value | R

esponsibility and uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Dependable room memory | A new volunteer searches by a production need, finds alternatives despite different vocabulary, sees local holds, checks fit, and leaves records a successor can understand. Continuity improves even if nothing is ever shared outside the room. | Record quality, backup, complete portability and clear conflict handling need sustained care. The room's willingness to do that work and the recurring benefit are not measured. |
| Cooperative wardrobe | A production worker requests pieces for dates; keepers selectively offer items, resolve conflicts, agree terms and record returns. People gain access to physical resources they do not own. | Consent, promises, transport, damage, loss and dispute responsibility must be agreed. One successful and one declined phone/paper exchange show both opportunity and a valid limit; neither group has opted into a service. |
| Living practice of reuse — recommended provisionally | A maker finds a past adaptation, understands its materials, reversibility and limits, tries an appropriate reuse, and optionally leaves an account the next maker can use. The value is a growing capacity to create with existing work. | Permission, attribution, contribution burden, contextual accuracy and long-term stewardship become product responsibilities. Stored notes do not establish successful transfer, and contribution may prove too costly. |

The recommendation connects the room's demonstrated usefulness to the broader creative intent in the brief. It sacrifices early investment in broad stock availability and automated exchange. It also chooses a risk: knowledge transfer has weaker capability evidence than local lookup. A more dependable catalogue alone may prove the better use of effort; that is an operator decision to revisit after discriminating evidence, not a conclusion this draft can settle. [E1–E4](evidence/observations.md), [C1–C6](evidence/capabilities.md)

Current alternatives

deserve equal treatment. Phone and paper already supported a loan; notebooks and direct teaching can preserve rich context with little software overhead; the desktop catalogue already finds some pieces. A new purchase may remain the appropriate creative or practical choice. Threadbank earns additional scope only if its benefit exceeds recording, coordination and maintenance effort. No competitive product survey is supplied or authorized here, so neither superiority over commercial products nor a market moat is established. The absence of funding and demand evidence applies equally to continued room-only investment and all expanded futures. [E2–E5](evidence/observations.md)

## The foundation we actually have

These classifications come from fictional stipulated receipts supplied in the packet. No application source was provided, and none of these tests was independently reproduced for this vision.

| Capability | Classification and implication |
|---|---|
| Local catalogue and photo lookup | **Working.** C1 records create, search and reopen after restart for 12 items. Preserve it; neither broad retrieval quality nor performance over the whole collection is established. |
| Reservation overlap warning | **Working with limitations.** C2 catches two overlapping holds for one item on one workstation. Manual exchange can leave another volunteer's view stale. Extend or clarify this behavior when needed; do not rebuild an allegedly absent warning. |
| JSON record export/import | **Working with limitations.** C3 preserves sampled descriptions and reservations; linked image bytes require separate copying. Build on this capability to improve a complete handoff. |
| Remote sharing access control | **Genuinely missing.** C4 establishes no remote service or permissions. Fitting notes remain in a separate operator-owned local file outside exported catalogue records. |
| Multi-group agreement | **Genuinely missing.** C5 establishes no shared consent, returns/loss rules or operatin

g owner. Synchronization cannot create those agreements. |
| Discoverable, reusable making knowledge | **Not established.** C6 confirms photographs and free text, not another maker's ability to discover, understand or adapt them. Validate transfer before proposing a large knowledge system. |

[Capability packet, C1–C6, 2026-10-21](evidence/capabilities.md)

Today's architecture is one local database, local photo files, manual record exchange and no account server. That is the present design, not an eternal deployment requirement. Offline usability for our room, exportability and private fitting notes are binding operator commitments. They remain binding through every horizon until the operator explicitly changes them. A future service cannot make local use depend on accounts or turn private notes into shared material by default. [Capability packet](evidence/capabilities.md), [brief](operator-brief.md)

## The ultimate experience, and what must be true

In the proposed future, a maker begins with a piece or an artistic intention. Threadbank offers relevant pieces and past transformations, with photographs, credited contributors, material context, reversible and irreversible steps, and known uncertainties. The maker judges relevance, checks condition and fit in person, and chooses whether to adapt, borrow through a separately agreed process, make anew or do nothing. The result is an informed creative choice and, optionally, a record that helps a future maker. The system does not certify fit, promise availability beyond its authority or decide the artistic outcome.

Value would mean more useful creative options, fewer unnecessary purchases or repeated mistakes, and less knowledge lost when volunteers leave. Usability requires both an inexperienced volunteer who can interpret a record and a busy maker who can contribute without writing an essay. Technical feasibility rests on understandable records and trustworthy local state before sophisticated discovery. Viability re

quires ongoing care within available time and resources; no willingness to pay, participation rate or sustainable shared-service model is established. [E1–E4](evidence/observations.md)

Working backward, that experience needs transferable examples; transferable examples need context and permission; useful discovery needs vocabulary that reflects how makers actually ask; reliable decisions need visible uncertainty about condition and promises; endurance needs portable records, maintained conventions and successors. The unresolved breakthrough is social as much as technical: can a small amount of documentation carry enough tacit craft knowledge to someone who was not there, without imposing more work than it saves?

## Useful horizons and their tests

### 1. Make the room's memory dependable

Preserve local lookup, overlap warnings and record exchange while extending the demonstrated gaps: finding a known item across vocabulary differences and handing over usable records with their photos. The independently valuable outcome is that another volunteer can retrieve and steward the collection with less reliance on personal memory.

A proposed end-to-end demonstration begins with representative room tasks, including the failed adjustable-garment case and new examples withheld from whoever prepares the records. An unfamiliar volunteer finds plausible pieces, interprets a local reservation warning, checks fit physically, and transfers records plus photos to a fresh offline workspace. Include restart, a missing-photo case and a stale manually exchanged reservation. The volunteer must see when a promise is unconfirmed and know whom to ask; this stage need not solve synchronization.

Observe the unchanged baseline first, including assistance, failed searches and total time spent maintaining descriptions. The new-capability demonstration must include the cross-vocabulary case or complete portable handoff that existing C1–C3 receipts do not establish; repeating those receipts alo

ne cannot pass. Exit when the intended workflow succeeds without the preparer's rescue and with correctly visible uncertainty, and the operator judges the upkeep acceptable. Reconsider an extension if gains disappear on held-out tasks, records silently lose photos, privacy is breached, or maintenance costs outweigh benefit. Preserve the working tool even if a proposed extension fails.

### 2. Make an adaptation transferable

Start with a few willing makers and permission-cleared examples from our room. A record should explain what changed, why, material and construction context, what can be undone, and what still requires personal judgment. This is a proposed minimum to test, not a settled schema. Capture can first use a simple template alongside existing records.

A second maker who did not author the example should be able to discover it, explain its limits, and attempt a suitable low-risk adaptation with the garment in hand. Compare with the present photograph/notebook/direct-conversation practice. Count author clarification and rescue as part of the cost, and preserve abandoned attempts rather than reporting only successful stories. Repeated cases with different authors and unfamiliar examples should establish whether transfer survives outside the initial demonstration. Physical inspection and maker judgment remain essential; records cannot establish suitability for an individual. [E3](evidence/observations.md)

Exit when makers can identify when an example applies and when it does not, the resulting work is useful, and authors find capture effort worth repeating. There is no justified universal time or success-rate target yet; agree tolerable effort with participants from the baseline before evaluating an extension. Stop expanding the record model if repeated success requires the original author to teach each case, permission is unclear, or contributors will not maintain it. Local histories can still help their own authors and successors. Whether that narrower

benefit changes the destination returns to the operator.

### 3. Sustain a living body of reusable craft

If transfer proves useful, invite participation beyond the first makers only with consent. People should be able to obtain and keep useful records, understand provenance and rights, correct or withdraw contributed material from channels we control, and continue local work when a distribution channel disappears. Withdrawal cannot guarantee recall of copies already legitimately exported; contributors need that limitation explained before sharing.

This horizon might use downloadable example collections, collaboration with a willing organization or a service with a named operator. Choose distribution from beneficiary evidence and stewardship capacity, not from a presumption that cloud hosting is progress. Independent value is durable craft knowledge and local continuity even if a broader network never emerges. Provisional continuation evidence includes repeated independent reuse, sustainable curation/support, genuine partner consent where relevant, and a successor able to operate or retire the chosen channel without stranding local records. Pause wider distribution if rights, upkeep or continuity cannot be supported.

Inter-room borrowing remains an optional branch requiring its own operator decision. Before making shared promises, groups would need an operating agreement, an accountable owner, agreed handling of stale availability and conflicts, and returns/loss procedures. A manually coordinated consenting pilot could test value before a service is built. Knowledge sharing must not quietly enroll anyone's physical collection. [E2](evidence/observations.md), [C4–C5](evidence/capabilities.md)

## Foundations that can endure

The proposed state boundaries are deliberately simple. Local catalogue records and original photos remain under the room's control. Private fitting notes stay separate and outside transferable catalogue or example records. A selected example is

a deliberately prepared derivative, with its own provenance and permission, rather than a copy of everything in the local database. Any future shared catalogue or publication channel owns only the state explicitly entrusted to it. Local holds and external offers must remain distinguishable; a stale warning cannot become an authoritative shared promise.

Export contracts should describe identifiers, versions and photo relationships clearly enough for restoration and another maintainer to understand. Complete portability must be demonstrated, not inferred from today's sampled JSON round trip. Changing the storage engine or adding remote synchronization is not presently justified by workload or failure evidence. First compare retaining the current design, a targeted export/discovery extension, and any proposed migration on actual retrieval, offline use, data compatibility, volunteer effort and maintenance. No latency, memory or scale measurements in this packet establish an architectural bottleneck. [C1–C4](evidence/capabilities.md)

Permissioned distribution, if selected later, introduces an actual trust boundary needing access policy, revocation behavior and operational ownership before private material crosses it. Public example collections may need editorial and rights controls without needing a remote account system; restricted sharing would require mechanisms genuinely absent today. Neither route may assume that a photograph is cleared merely because it is already stored locally.

Costly commitments include published content rights, permanent-service promises and formats that strand records. Prefer reversible trials, explicit permissions and replaceable distribution channels. Preserve simple local recovery instructions and train a successor alongside feature work. Record failed retrieval, misunderstood examples, stale promises and human interventions without collecting private fitting information as telemetry. The proposed instrumentation can begin with a consen

ted observation log; continuous remote tracking is not necessary.

## Adoption, resources and learning

Two volunteers can start by observing real work and preparing a small transfer exercise. They cannot credibly promise continuous operation of a shared service. Useful feedback, documentation and succession should progress alongside technical extensions. Capture and vocabulary experiments can run in parallel with portable-handoff improvements; a large discovery interface should wait until examples demonstrably transfer. External distribution depends on permissions and a sustainable caretaker. Borrowing additionally depends on governance, regardless of technical readiness.

Nonfinancial returns include continuity, creative autonomy, less waste and open contribution. Financial value could include avoided purchases or paid support, but neither net savings nor income is proven. Possible grants, partners or paid services are funding hypotheses, not commitments. Any offer should be tested for whether it covers support and stewardship costs while preserving offline use and export. Free contribution still consumes time. If funding never appears, local usefulness and exportable examples can remain worthwhile; deciding which work to sustain belongs to the operator. [E1, E4](evidence/observations.md)

A proportionate observation period should cover preparation, actual use and post-production return/handoff, then revisit a later production for delayed errors and maintenance burden. Track successful and failed retrieval, avoided purchases only when attributed and checked, contributor/keeper time, rescue by knowledgeable people, adaptation usefulness, privacy errors and unreconciled promises. These are proposed observations, not current results. A short trial cannot establish long-term retention, lifetime savings or broad demand.

The cheapest discriminating next research is an observed retrieval/handoff with another volunteer, followed by an independent maker using a small perm

ission-cleared adaptation record. The first tests whether improving continuity earns its upkeep; the second tests the recommended destination itself. A willing group interview or manually negotiated exchange can investigate the alternative borrowing future without assuming consent. Discovery of low contribution appetite, little independent reuse, excessive stewardship cost or a stronger beneficiary need should trigger a new operator choice. More money or specialists could accelerate separate experiments and improve privacy/design review; they cannot manufacture willingness to contribute or remove the need for repeated real use.

## Ordered immediate advances

1. **Preserve and establish the comparison.** Retain working lookup, limited overlap warnings and export/import. Observe representative retrieval and an offline handoff, including failures and help. This comes first because improvements need an honest baseline; a small sample of receipts cannot establish room-wide reliability. Continue only with a clear beneficiary problem and an agreed tolerable upkeep burden.
2. **Extend continuity where evidence points.** Test vocabulary cues against the adjustable-garment miss and held-out tasks; extend the existing export path toward complete records-and-photo handoff and explicit missing-file reporting. Keep stale reservation uncertainty visible. These directly support the room now and provide the dependable foundation for future examples; broaden engineering only if observed failures justify it.
3. **Investigate transfer before building broad discovery.** With willing makers, prepare permission-cleared adaptations and observe another maker using them. This can proceed alongside the limited continuity work. The gap is unestablished transfer, not absent notes. Continue toward structured discovery only if useful independent interpretation and repeatable contribution emerge.
4. **Validate stewardship before wider reach.** Rehearse a successor taking over records and maintena

nce; explore distribution and funding with actual willing participants only after useful examples exist. A named caretaker, rights and support boundaries precede wider obligations. Any physical exchange system returns separately to the operator for consent and responsibility decisions.

These advances describe the next useful decisions, not an authorized backlog. The open strategic decisions are whether to adopt this destination, how to order personal usefulness, volunteer benefit, openness and income, and whether any later relationship beyond our room warrants its added responsibilities. The roadmap changes as evidence arrives; commitments change only by explicit operator choice.

# Threadbank: A room whose craft survives its volunteers

Provisional, not adopted. **Threadbank helps each new volunteer find, reserve and care for a suitable garment, understand its provenance, and leave reliable records for the next person.** The operator-selected destination is dependable stewardship for our own costume room: a collection whose usefulness and craft survive changes of volunteers and maintainers.

Begin with dependable catalogue handovers, extend that foundation through the whole production cycle, then sustain it across volunteer generations. Each horizon delivers value even if the next never happens. Offline room use and export remain commitments; the desktop is the current implementation. Replaceable interfaces should leave later choices possible without turning this vision into a shared service. Cross-group exchange and a public creative network are not the chosen destination; changing that direction belongs to the operator.

## Why this future matters

A costume room's memory lives partly in garments, partly in records and partly in people. Threadbank should make the records useful when the person who remembers is absent. In the supplied account, one volunteer found a coat quickly and photographs helped a director choose two candidates; fit was checked in person. Another search failed because descriptions used different vocabulary. The operator attributes one avoided purchase to the tool, but no repeated timing or savings study exists ([observations, E1](evidence/observations.md)). The pivotal opportunity is continuity of useful knowledge and trustworthy promises, rather than simply more catalogue entries.

The ambitious end experience is an incoming volunteer taking a production from first search through reservation, fitting, permitted alteration, care and return, then passing that history to a successor without relying on the creator's memory. Threadbank supplies candidates, records, visible uncertainty and recoverable handovers. People judg

e fit, authorize alterations, resolve conflicting promises and decide what personal information belongs in a record. A blank field never establishes consent.

The chosen scope favors a quiet, understandable tool and continuity over wider reach. Its possible value includes less searching and duplicate making, fewer damaged relationships over promises, preservation of craft, and perhaps fewer purchases. Those are hypotheses to examine, not measured benefits. Stewardship can sustain value through habitual use, clear ownership and inexpensive recovery; no market moat, willingness to pay or funding offer is established. The maintainer cannot promise a permanent shared service alone, and continued room investment also needs evidence of use and tolerable upkeep ([E2–E5](evidence/observations.md)). Phone, paper and notebooks remain useful fallbacks and comparison baselines. No product landscape survey was authorized or performed.

A successor should locate a suitable candidate, see the latest known reservation information and its limits, find the associated photograph, and recover the transferred collection without the creator present. This is useful even if broader production support never arrives.

### 2. A production leaves the room ready for its successor

Extend reliable handover through reservation, fitting decisions, permitted alteration, care and return. A volunteer sees what is known about an item and what still needs human confirmation. The next production can understand its condition and commitments instead of reconstructing them from scattered memory. That improved readiness is valuable independently of any later knowledge library.

The dependency is the first horizon's record identity and exchange discipline. In parallel, work with volunteers to decide the minimum useful condition, provenance and care information, who maintains it, and where consent is recorded. Try a small real production workflow before adding extensive fields: compare missing or contradictory records, volunteer effort, unplanned purchases and human rescues with current practice. Do not attribute purchase changes to Threadbank without examining availability, fit and production differences.

Advance when incoming volunteers can use the returned records, owners' restrictions remain visible, and upkeep remains acceptable through a production and return cycle. Reconsider the fields or workflow if entries are routinely deferred, sensitive notes leak into shared records, or the application creates confident but incorrect guidance. In-person fit and permission decisions remain human responsibilities. No calendar deadline or savings target is established by the evidence.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented in this file and in
the individual wave records under [`docs/waves/`](docs/waves/).

The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).
This project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Changed

- Envision develops concrete product futures before recommending an open destination and delivers one coherent vision by default, with research in the argument and detailed review accounting in the response. A compact saved status distinguishes reviewed revisions, pending findings and later edits. A shorter strategic core loads four local phase companions at their point of use; install/upgrade guidance carries the complete set, preserving customizations and stopping conflicts. Advisory review sharpens scope and evidence challenges while retaining its bounded repair/verification rule and operator-owned strategy. Wave 220a9 / change 220a8; these are instruction changes, not a claim of general authoring superiority.

## [1.39.0] - 2026-10-29

### Added

- Envision project / `wf-envision` defines an ambitious product vision and an adaptable long-horizon roadmap, with useful technical and nontechnical advances and proportionate advisory reviews. Its opening makes the destination clear; distant horizons retain advancement conditions without invented precision. Decision-relevant research and validation of existing capabilities ground ordered immediate advances, including enabling technical changes where justified; technical shifts require causal evidence and alternatives rather than assumed technology benefits. It distinguishes transformative destination, unresolved breakthroughs and useful stages without silently shrinking earlier ambition. Advisory coverage uses product strategy, domain/application workflow, senior architecture and independent challenge, with consequential specialties and optional archetype techniques or an explicitly request

ed Council. Plan change conditionally carries an explicitly adopted vision’s relevant outcomes and prerequisites without editing it. Seed 100 authors missing prompts; seed 160 guides changed-seed179 and seed170 reconciliation into existing prompts, preserving project additions and stopping conflicts. Subsequent rendering emits the skill for active hosts. Authoring grants no implementation authority. Waves 21u1e / 21tpc, 21tpp / 21vpo, 21y6d / 21xpg and 21xq1 / 21xq0; authoring evidence is case-specific, and the 21ux4 comparison did not establish superiority.

## [1.38.0] - 2026-10-26

### Added

- Each wave has a shared, gitignored `.wavefoundry/work/<wave-id>/` area for temporary work and review aids. Successful operator-authorized whole-wave closure attempts contained cleanup of that wave's owned generation; dry-runs and failed closes preserve it. Unique evidence must be retained before cleanup. Wave 21luh / 21luf.
- Readiness diagnostics identify changed plan sections. Focused re-review can show each lane the cumulative changes since its own approval, using optional reviewed-text snapshots; missing or unusable snapshots fall back explicitly to full review. Approval authority and invalidation rules are unchanged. Wave 21luh / 21lug.
- Framework maintainers can inspect and accept a complete passing test run rejected solely for eligible, explicitly reviewed bookkeeping changes. Acceptance preserves the original failed record and records the exact exception without rerunning workers; substantive changes and failed tests remain refused. Wave 21k15 / 21lue.
- While a long-running dashboard is using index code older than what is installed, every view shows a notice saying so and that restarting the dashboard fixes it. The notice clears after a restart. The dashboard never restarts itself, and the index-compatibility guard is unchanged. Wave 21s7b / 21s7a.
- Codex now gets explicit-invocation metadata for the operator-only Wavefoundry skills: rendering writes `agents/ope

nai.yaml` with `policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false` beside those skills in the active `.codex/skills` and `.agents/skills` folders. This guides skill selection; it does not grant or restrict tool access. Claude skills and `SKILL.md` content are unchanged, and custom metadata files are preserved. Wave 21fgr / 21fgq.

### Changed

- Prepare and Review wave now judge intent fit. The council-chair reports `intent_fit` at readiness (would meeting the Requirements and ACs establish each change's Product Intent and the wave Objective, and can the measure of success be read) and at delivery. On every delivery review, the coordinator drafts a dated `Intent outcome:` paragraph in `## Review Checkpoints`, and new wave records include that heading. Assign the independent check to `qa-reviewer` when it is in the current required delivery roster; otherwise assign one reviewer already in that roster. If the roster is empty, record `No independent delivery-lane intent check ran` in `## Review Checkpoints`; do not add a lane or claim an independent check occurred. The assigned reviewer independently confirms or corrects the outcome; a required delivery Council reuses that assessment when available. Close adds only the non-blocking advisory described below. Wave 21j63 / 21j62.
- New council approvals carry an intent verdict. Readiness refuses a verdict that the plan will not achieve its intent; delivery can honestly record an unmet intent and surface it for operator signoff without trapping the wave. Existing ledgers remain valid. Wave 21j63 / 21kk5.
- Reload and upgrade now retire context-efficiency pending rows for wave ids that match no wave record and have had no activity for 30 days. Their telemetry is kept, any new event makes them pending again, and the result lists them in `retired_orphan_waves`. Nothing is retired when wave records cannot be read reliably. Wave 21s1u / 21s1t.
- An operator sign-off no longer claims test evidence the operator never produced. Record it wi

thout `integrity_checks`: the five checks are stored as `null` (not applicable) with a not-applicable detection method, and agents no longer ask the operator for check values. An operator who did check may state `true`, `false` or `null` for each one. `null` is refused on every other record, specialist and council approvals must still affirm all five checks, and existing ledgers keep their original values. Waves 21sld / 21qbb and 21s6f / 21s53.

### Fixed

- Source-history qualification tests respect configured live and archive record roots under renamed profiles, excluding historical records from the active-carrier census while still validating archived ledgers. Wave 21u6x / 21szl.
- MCP reload pauses monitor callbacks before cleanup and preserves workers and handler resources if preparation cannot finish. Cleanup failures are explicit, shutdown closes the current handler, and process diagnostics distinguish an implementation reload from a host restart. Wave 21uny / 21ttt.
- Owned wave work remains available across device renumbering when its recorded nonzero inode still matches. Invalid ownership remains preserved, and checks against substitution during an operation stay strict. Wave 21w0b / 21vug.
- Setup reports the process's bounded provider-selection reason and stops before incompatible or narrowly unverified implicit local fallback preparation for an existing index. Qualified Tensorwell avoids local preparation; explicit local settings, fresh or legacy indexes and deliberate full rebuilds retain their supported paths. The final indexer precision guard remains authoritative, and setup never silently converts an update into a rebuild. Wave 21kbd / 21kbc.
- A long-running MCP server no longer spends most of a CPU core on context-efficiency projection. The background monitor attempts a closed or unknown pending wave once per pending generation instead of on every 15-second tick, and a retryable failure now waits out the quiet period. Hard-boundary projection is u

nchanged. Wave 21s91 / 21s90.
- Reopening a wave by its short id now unseals and focuses the wave's full folder id, so its context-efficiency telemetry no longer lands on a short-id key that never publishes. Reload and upgrade retire existing short-id alias rows (keeping their telemetry) and list them in `retired_alias_waves`. Wave 21s8v / 21s8u.
- The dashboard's Index dialog no longer reports an index it is refusing to read as "not built". It shows the refusal and its recovery action (restart the dashboard); a missing index still reads "not built". Wave 21s7b / 21s79.
- The dashboard's Index tile, Graph view and Index dialog now give the same explanation and recovery action when the index is refused or a graph publication is in progress, and the Graph view updates when that state changes. MCP tool responses are unchanged. Wave 21rft / 21rf7.
- `wf_audit` no longer reports three valid non-tool identifiers (configuration, package-path and error names) as stale tool references. Unknown tool references are still reported. Wave 21fgr / 21fgp.

The dashboard is still started with its output discarded and detached, uncha

nged on Windows. Wave 21ilh / 21ilg.
- A dashboard started with `--port 0` now records and prints the port it actually bound, instead of a URL ending in `:0/`. Wave 21ilh / 21ilg.

### Changed

Wave 21cw4 / 21cw5.

### Fixed

- Upgrades on native Windows no longer refuse with "verified private pack changed before validation". Python's handle and path stat calls can report different ctimes for the same file there, so every pack identity check that compares a handle stat with a path stat now ignores ctime and still compares every other field it compared before (inode, size and mtime, plus device where it was checked). Checks between two stats of the same kind, and the recorded five-field proof, are unchanged. An upgrade is staged by the installed runner, so a Windows repository that patched this locally keeps that patch until this release is installed. Wave 21cw4 / 21alh.
- The Claude Code pre-edit hook lets the read-only Grep and Glob tools search seed and framework paths while the edit gates are closed; edit tools stay gated. Repositories receive the updated hook when setup or upgrade re-renders platform surfaces. Wave 21cw4 / 21ayv.
- `wf setup` refuses a root that has no `.wavefoundry/framework/` folder before doing anything else, exits non-zero, and names `--root`; `--check`, `--check-gpu` and `--help` are unchanged. A framework folder reached through a link is still accepted. Wave 21cw4 / 21ayw.
- Rendering refuses a carrier destination that is a dangling link, or whose ancestor folder is one, and any destination that resolves inside the repository's `.git` folder (compared case-insensitively on every platform), instead of creating the file at the link's targ

et. Docs-lint reports such a destination as a finding instead of failing. Other links inside the repository behave as before. Wave 21cw4 / 21ayx.
- `wf_close_change` refuses an ambiguous wave record before any gate or write: an id recorded more than once, a record with more than one status line (fenced or not, including an unreadable one), or a record started by a fenced id line. Fenced `Depends On:` examples stay ignored, and `wf_close_wave` is unchanged. Wave 21cw4 / 21cw2.
- The Tensorwell controller check compares its open-file and path snapshots without ctime, matching the pack identity fix, so it cannot refuse an unchanged controller when handle and path stats disagree on ctime alone; replacing, resizing or rewriting the controller is still refused. Wave 21bzn / 21bzm.
- The profile shortcut tests read the colliding prompt names from the default table instead of literals, so a source-rebranded distribution can run them unchanged. Wave 21cw4 / 21cw3.
